summary:
This attempt (implementation attempt 5, review cycle 3) resolves fix-request-review-3.md's single `major` finding against the cycle-3/review-3 worktree state, without touching anything else. The finding: `CreateAccountUseCase`'s duplicate-phone check (`existsByProviderAndIdentifier`, create-account.use-case.ts:96) is a preflight read, not a lock — two concurrent `POST /auth/register` requests for the same phone can both pass it before either commits. The database's partial unique index (`UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier`) is the real source of truth and correctly rejects the loser's INSERT, but `TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save()` previously let that raw `QueryFailedError` propagate unchanged, and `GlobalExceptionFilter` maps any exception it doesn't recognize (including `QueryFailedError`) to a generic HTTP 500 — so the loser of the race got an opaque server error instead of the AC46-required `phone_already_exists`/409 business error, even though the losing transaction itself still rolled back correctly (no partial state was ever left; only the *reported status code* was wrong). Fixed by adding a `translateUniqueViolation` step inside `TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save()` (`libs/modules/identity-access/src/infrastructure/persistence/typeorm-auth-identity.repository.ts`): it catches `QueryFailedError`, checks the wrapped Postgres driver error for SQLSTATE `23505` (unique_violation) against the named constraint `UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier`, and if both match, throws `DomainError.conflict('phone_already_exists', ...)` — the exact error `GlobalExceptionFilter` already maps to 409, and the identical code/message the preflight check already throws for the non-racy case. Any other `QueryFailedError` (unrelated constraint, unrelated table) is rethrown unchanged, so this only narrows the one specific race, not error handling generally. This repository method is shared by both `CreateAccountUseCase` (registration/admin account creation) and `ChangeAccountPhoneUseCase` (which has the exact same TOCTOU shape with its own `existsByProviderAndIdentifier` preflight, change-account-phone.use-case.ts:50-53), so the fix closes the race for both call sites, not only registration, without touching either use case's code. Added a new, real-Postgres e2e test to `apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` — 'lets exactly one of two concurrent registrations for the same phone succeed, rejecting the other with a 409 business error and no partial state' — that fires two concurrent `POST /auth/register` requests with the same phone through the real HTTP layer, asserts the response statuses are exactly `[201, 409]` (never 500) with the loser's body carrying `errorCode: 'phone_already_exists'`, then queries the real `AccountRepository`/`AuthIdentityRepository`/`UserProfileRepository`/`AccountRoleRepository` (already exported from each module's public-api.ts by a prior attempt) to confirm the winner has exactly one committed `AuthIdentity`/`UserProfile`/`AccountRole` graph, and finally logs in with the registered credentials end to end to prove the committed account is fully usable. Every deterministic validation command was re-run from a clean shell against the live worktree and real infrastructure (memories-test-postgres) after this change: lint, typecheck, unit tests (unchanged: 54 suites/244 tests — this fix touches only infrastructure/e2e code, no new unit-testable logic was introduced beyond what the e2e test already exercises against the real database), build, architecture (0 violations, 390 modules), migration run+revert+run, and the full e2e suite (6 suites/42 tests, up from 6/41 — the one new concurrency test), plus every skill-required deterministic check script. No other file, use case, or already-passed criterion from the prior cycle-3/review-2-fix submission was touched.

Prior attempts (preserved for context):

Attempt 4 #1 (AC47): the centralized password policy referenced by task.md §19 did not actually exist — `RegisterDto`, `CreateAccountDto` and `ChangeAccountPasswordDto` each hard-coded their own `@MinLength(8)`/`@MaxLength(255)`, and neither `CreateAccountUseCase` nor `ChangeAccountPasswordUseCase` validated password length at all, so any caller invoking those use cases directly (bypassing HTTP DTO validation) could hash and persist an out-of-policy password. Fixed by adding one new module, `libs/modules/identity-access/src/domain/value-objects/password-policy.ts`, exporting `PASSWORD_POLICY` (MIN_LENGTH/MAX_LENGTH constants) and `assertPasswordPolicy()` (throws `DomainError.validation`, mapped to HTTP 400 by the existing `GlobalExceptionFilter` — the same status a DTO-level failure already produced). All three DTOs now derive their `@MinLength`/`@MaxLength` decorator arguments from `PASSWORD_POLICY` instead of duplicating the literals, and `CreateAccountUseCase.execute`/`ChangeAccountPasswordUseCase.execute` both call `assertPasswordPolicy()` before hashing, inside the transaction, so the policy is enforced at the application/domain boundary regardless of caller. New unit coverage: `password-policy.spec.ts` (boundary values, and that the thrown error never echoes the password), plus new negative-path tests in `create-account.use-case.spec.ts` and a new `change-account-password.use-case.spec.ts` (didn't exist before this attempt) proving each use case rejects and persists nothing for a policy-violating password. #2 (AC51): the only prior 'transaction' tests used a mocked `UnitOfWork` whose fake `withTransaction` just calls the callback inline, so they could prove step *sequencing* but never a real rollback. Added `apps/api/test/register-transaction-rollback.e2e-spec.ts`, a real-Postgres e2e spec that boots the full `AppModule` with `USER_PROFILE_PROVISIONER` overridden (via Nest's `overrideProvider`) to record the `accountId` it was called with and then reject — forcing `CreateAccountUseCase`'s real transaction to fail on its last write (§8 step 6) after Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole have already been written in the same transaction — then queries the same real repositories the app itself uses (`AccountRepository.findById`/`findByIdIncludingDeleted`, `AuthIdentityRepository.findAllByAccountId`, `AccountRoleRepository.listRoleIdsForAccount`, `UserProfileRepository.existsByAccountId`) by that captured id and asserts all four are absent. This required exporting `ACCOUNT_REPOSITORY`/`AccountRepository` and `AUTH_IDENTITY_REPOSITORY`/`AuthIdentityRepository` from identity-access's `public-api.ts`, and `USER_PROFILE_REPOSITORY`/`UserProfileRepository` from user-profiles' `public-api.ts` — following the exact precedent already set by `ACCOUNT_ROLE_REPOSITORY`/`ROLE_REPOSITORY` being exported there for the same test-only reason. Every deterministic validation command was re-run from a clean shell against the live worktree and real infrastructure (memories-test-postgres) after these changes: lint, typecheck, unit tests (54 suites/244 tests, up from 52/236 — the three new spec files), build, architecture (0 violations, 390 modules), migration run+revert+run, and the full e2e suite (6 suites/41 tests, up from 5/40 — the new rollback spec), plus every skill-required deterministic check script. No other file from the prior cycle-3/review-1-fix submission was touched. Cycle 3 itself resumed a worktree that already contained a substantially complete MEMORIES-0002 backend (Account/AuthIdentity/UserProfile/RBAC/JWT/portal-authorization/request-context/audit/CRUD) with all 9 blockers/majors from changes-review fix-request-review-1.md already fixed in-place (verified by direct code inspection plus check_auth_invariants.py/check_port_bindings.py/check_module_wiring.py, not re-implemented). This cycle's net-new work is the changes/cycle-002 addendum: public self-registration `POST /auth/register` (RegisterDto, RegisterUseCase, RegisterResponseDto, AuthController wiring, module registration, unit tests, e2e tests, docs). RegisterUseCase composes the existing CreateAccountUseCase (§8 transaction, unchanged) and then issues a PUBLIC-portal session the same way LoginUseCase does, so a successful registration returns an access token + refresh cookie equivalent to a PUBLIC login for the account just created, with no client-controllable portal/role/permission/accountId. This continuation (attempt 2, after the prior attempt was marked failed) re-ran every deterministic validation command from scratch against the live worktree rather than trusting the prior self-report: lint, typecheck, unit test (52 suites/236 tests), build, architecture (0 violations/385 modules), migration run+revert+run against real Postgres, and the full real-infrastructure e2e suite. All four e2e specs now pass, including apps/api/test/media-upload-flow.e2e-spec.ts, which the prior cycle's self-report had marked failing on a local EADDRINUSE :::9464 conflict — that port was free on re-verification (lsof confirmed no listener), so the failure was confirmed transient/environmental as suspected, not a code defect, and AC40 is now fully passed rather than partial. Spot-checked source for fix-request-review-1 items #1, #2 and #8 directly (JwtAuthGuard's live ACCOUNT_LOOKUP-backed status/tokenVersion check with the DI token genuinely wired in identity-access.module.ts; PortalGuard + RequirePortal('ADMIN') on UserProfileController; only status/phone/password PATCH routes on AccountController, no generic no-op PATCH) to confirm the prior cycle's claims were not fabricated. Review cycle 1 (codex) then returned one `major` finding — AC50 failed because `POST /auth/register` only declared its 201 Swagger response, omitting the reachable 400/403/409/429 error outcomes. Fixed by adding a shared `ErrorResponseDto` next to `GlobalExceptionFilter` (the same envelope every route's non-2xx response already uses), documenting all four error statuses with `@ApiResponse` on `AuthController.register`, and — since the `verify-openapi-contract` skill's deterministic checker (`check_openapi_contract.py`) had never actually been run in this task before, a real gap this cycle closes — creating the worktree-root `openapi-contracts.json` manifest plus a new generated-document contract test (`apps/api/test/openapi-contract.e2e-spec.ts`) that builds the real `buildOpenApiDocument()` output and asserts exactly `[201, 400, 403, 409, 429]` are documented for the route. No other files from the prior cycle-3 submission were touched.

decisions.decision: Translated the Postgres unique-violation for `UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier` into `DomainError.conflict('phone_already_exists', ...)` inside `TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save()` (a new private `translateUniqueViolation` helper wrapping the existing `save()` body in try/catch), rather than adding a database-level advisory lock, a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` before the preflight check, or a retry loop in `CreateAccountUseCase`.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-3.md's finding is specifically that the *reported error* is wrong (500 instead of 409) for the race's loser, not that the race itself is unsafe — the database's partial unique index already prevents any duplicate row from ever committing, and `UnitOfWork.withTransaction`'s existing catch/rollback/rethrow already rolls back the loser's transaction cleanly on any thrown error, DomainError or not. Locking or retrying would add real complexity (lock scope/timeout tuning, retry-storm risk under contention) to fix a problem that is purely about status-code translation, not data integrity — the persistence layer is the one place both call sites (`CreateAccountUseCase` and `ChangeAccountPhoneUseCase`, which has the identical TOCTOU shape) already funnel through, so fixing it there closes the gap for both without touching either use case.

decisions.decision: Matched on both the Postgres SQLSTATE (`23505` unique_violation) and the named constraint (`UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier`) before translating, using `error.driverError.code`/`error.driverError.constraint` (TypeORM's `QueryFailedError` also copies these onto the error instance itself, but `driverError` is the documented/stable place to read them from), instead of matching on SQLSTATE alone or on the error message text.
decisions.reason: `identity.auth_identities` has a second unique index (`UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_subject`) that also raises `23505` for a completely different conflict (duplicate social-provider subject) — matching on SQLSTATE alone would silently mislabel that violation as `phone_already_exists` too. Message-text matching is fragile across Postgres versions/locales. Constraint-name matching is exact and is already how the migration itself names the index (`libs/platform/database/src/migrations/1722540000000-CreateIdentityAccessSchema.ts`), so the repository's constant references the same authoritative name rather than duplicating a magic string with no shared source of truth.

decisions.decision: Added the concurrency regression test to the existing `describe('register (changes/cycle-002 addendum)', ...)` block in `apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` (reusing that file's existing `nextPhone()`/`login()` helpers and newly-added repository handles) rather than creating a new spec file or adding a mocked-repository unit test for the new `translateUniqueViolation` branch.
decisions.reason: The bug is a genuine database race — a mocked `AuthIdentityRepository`/mocked `QueryFailedError` unit test would only prove the translation function's if/else logic, not that a real concurrent Postgres write actually reaches it, which is exactly what fix-request-review-3.md's evidence says the *existing* E2E coverage failed to exercise ('only submits the duplicate after the first account has committed'). No `TypeOrmXxxRepository` class in this codebase has its own unit-test file (verified: `libs/modules/identity-access/test/` contains only domain/application-layer specs) — infra-layer repository behavior is exercised exclusively through E2E/integration tests against real Postgres throughout this codebase, so a new unit spec here would be inconsistent with established convention, not filling a real gap.

decisions.decision: Verified all 9 items in fix-request-review-1.md against the current worktree before writing any code, and found #1-#8 already correctly fixed (JwtAuthGuard live account-status/tokenVersion check, PortalGuard on UserProfileController, atomic revokeIfActive CAS on refresh, userProfileId preserved across refresh, OriginGuard on /auth/refresh, ambient RequestContext.currentActorId() for all audit actors, dateOnlyTransformer on UserProfileOrmEntity.dateOfBirth, fake generic PATCH /accounts/:id removed entirely with no dangling references).
decisions.reason: The docstrings and code at each cited file:line already state and implement exactly the fix each item demands, and check_auth_invariants.py/check_port_bindings.py/check_module_wiring.py all pass — re-implementing already-correct code would violate 'triển khai thay đổi nhỏ nhất' and risk regressing working fixes.

decisions.decision: Implemented POST /auth/register as a new RegisterUseCase that injects and calls CreateAccountUseCase directly (constructor DI on the concrete provider class) instead of duplicating the §8 transaction.
decisions.reason: changes/cycle-002/requirement-addendum.md explicitly requires reusing the existing §8 transaction rather than re-declaring it; CreateAccountUseCase already has an existing unit test ('stamps a null actor for an unauthenticated self-registration (no RequestContext store)') anticipating exactly this reuse.

decisions.decision: RegisterUseCase issues the PUBLIC-portal session in a second, separate UnitOfWork.withTransaction call after CreateAccountUseCase's transaction has already committed, rather than trying to nest one transaction inside another.
decisions.reason: CreateAccountUseCase owns and commits its own transaction; RefreshSessionUseCase already establishes the precedent of issuing tokens/sessions in their own transaction, separate from the account-creation transaction.

decisions.decision: Hardcoded tokenVersion: 0 on the access token RegisterUseCase issues, instead of re-reading the just-created Account.
decisions.reason: CreateAccountUseCase always creates new Accounts with tokenVersion: 0 (visible in its own source); avoids an extra DB round trip for a value that cannot differ.

decisions.decision: No new guard or rate-limit decorator added to the /auth/register route.
decisions.reason: The route must be reachable by an unauthenticated caller by definition (no guard), and ThrottlerGuard is already registered globally via APP_GUARD in SecurityModule so every route, including this new one, is throttled identically to /auth/login without additional code — verified the existing rate-limit.e2e-spec.ts still passes.

decisions.decision: Did not re-implement any of the fix-request-review-1 items or the register endpoint; instead re-ran every deterministic validation command (lint, typecheck, unit test, build, architecture, migration up/down/up, full test:e2e, and all three skill-required check scripts) from a clean shell in this continuation before writing anything to implementation.json.
decisions.reason: The continuation protocol flagged the previous attempt as 'failed' despite a prior implementation.json already claiming success; rather than trust that self-report, every validation claim was independently reproduced against the live worktree and real infra (memories-test-postgres/redis/minio), plus targeted source reads for fix-request items #1, #2 and #8. This turned up one stale claim (media-upload-flow.e2e-spec.ts EADDRINUSE) that no longer reproduced — port 9464 was free this run — so AC40 was upgraded from partial to passed with updated evidence; no other discrepancies were found.

decisions.decision: Fixed review cycle 1's sole `major` finding (AC50) by adding a single shared `ErrorResponseDto` (in `global-exception.filter.ts`, next to the `ErrorResponseBody` interface it mirrors) and four `@ApiResponse` decorators (400/403/409/429) on `AuthController.register`, instead of a bespoke error DTO per status or per controller.
decisions.reason: Every route already funnels through the one global `GlobalExceptionFilter`, so its envelope (`statusCode`/`errorCode`/`message`/`correlationId`, `stack` excluded as non-production-only) is the real, shared runtime contract for every non-2xx response — one reusable Swagger DTO for it is correct per the verify-openapi-contract skill ('Reuse one shared error DTO when the runtime envelope is shared'), not scope creep, and leaves it available for any future controller without re-deriving the shape.

decisions.decision: Wrote all five `@ApiResponse({...})` decorators on `AuthController.register` as single-line object literals instead of the more readable multi-line form used in the first draft.
decisions.reason: `check_openapi_contract.py`'s handler-boundary scan (`prefix.rfind("\n  }")`) locates the previous handler's closing brace by string search, and a multi-line decorator's own closing `\n  })` is indistinguishable from that boundary marker, silently truncating the extracted decorator block down to nothing useful. Every existing `@ApiResponse` in this codebase (account.controller.ts, the rest of auth.controller.ts) is already single-line for the same reason, so this matches, rather than deviates from, established convention.

decisions.decision: Scoped the new `openapi-contracts.json` manifest to exactly the one operation the review flagged (`POST /api/v1/auth/register`), not every existing controller route.
decisions.reason: No other route's Swagger documentation was found deficient by review — account.controller.ts and the rest of auth.controller.ts also only document their success status today, but AC50 (the only failing criterion) is scoped to registration, and task/addendum text does not require retrofitting every pre-existing endpoint's error contract in this cycle. Expanding the manifest to routes with no matching error decorators would just make `check_openapi_contract.py` fail for out-of-scope operations. `ai/agents/claude-implementer.md`'s 'không mở rộng scope nếu chưa có trong task/addendum' applies; a broader OpenAPI error-contract pass across the whole API is future work, not this fix.

decisions.decision: Named the new contract test `apps/api/test/openapi-contract.e2e-spec.ts` (not the `openapi-contract.spec.ts` name shown as an illustrative example in the skill's `manifest.md`) and pointed the manifest's `contract_test` field at that same path.
decisions.reason: `./test/jest-e2e.json`'s `testRegex` only matches `*.e2e-spec.ts`; a `*.spec.ts` file under `apps/api/test/` would never actually run as part of `npm run test:e2e`, silently failing to be the real, executed contract test the skill requires ('Runtime E2E tests alone are insufficient' cuts the other way too — an unrun test is worse than insufficient, it's decorative).

decisions.decision: Modeled the centralized password policy as a plain exported constant (`PASSWORD_POLICY`) plus a free function (`assertPasswordPolicy`) in `domain/value-objects/password-policy.ts`, rather than a `ValueObject<Password>` wrapping the plaintext (the shape used by `PhoneNumber`/`phone-number.vo.ts`) or a DI-injected port/service (the shape used by `PhoneNormalizerPort`).
decisions.reason: `ValueObject`'s base class (`libs/shared/kernel/src/value-objects/value-object.ts`) has no `toJSON`/redaction override — wrapping a plaintext password in one would mean any accidental `JSON.stringify`/logging of that object leaks the password, which task.md §19 ('Không log credential') and the implement-auth-security-change skill both forbid; a plain string-in, throw-or-return-void function never holds the plaintext anywhere after it returns. A DI port (like `PhoneNormalizerPort`) is unnecessary because there is no infrastructure dependency to keep out of `domain` — the policy is pure length arithmetic, so a plain function is enough and needs no provider registration, keeping `check_port_bindings.py`/`check_module_wiring.py` output unchanged.

decisions.decision: Enforced `assertPasswordPolicy()` inside `CreateAccountUseCase`'s and `ChangeAccountPasswordUseCase`'s existing `unitOfWork.withTransaction` callback, immediately before the existing `passwordHasher.hash(...)` call, rather than at the top of `execute()` before the transaction starts.
decisions.reason: Keeps every input-validation step for this transaction in one place matching the transaction's own step order (task.md §8: normalize phone -> check duplicate -> hash password), so a reader scanning the transaction body sees the policy check exactly where the password is about to be consumed; also means a directly-invoked use case (bypassing DTO validation) fails fast with the identical `DomainError.validation` (HTTP 400) shape whether the violation is caught by class-validator or by this check, with no double-transaction-open/rollback semantics to reason about.

decisions.decision: Wrote `apps/api/test/register-transaction-rollback.e2e-spec.ts` to override `USER_PROFILE_PROVISIONER` with `Test.createTestingModule(...).overrideProvider(...).useValue(...)` rather than (a) reusing the existing mocked-`UnitOfWork` unit-test style, (b) adding a test-only failure-injection flag to `CreateAccountUseCase` itself, or (c) trying to force a real Postgres-level failure (e.g. a constraint violation) at the UserProfile-provisioning step.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-2.md #2 explicitly asked for a real *database-backed* test proving *rollback*, which a mocked `UnitOfWork` can never demonstrate (its fake `withTransaction` just calls the callback inline, never opening or rolling back a real transaction) — ruling out (a). Adding a failure-injection flag/hook to production code (b) would be scope creep purely for testability and risks a real code path silently depending on test-only branching. Nest's `overrideProvider` is the framework-supported way to substitute one collaborator in an otherwise-real, otherwise-fully-wired `AppModule` — every other write in the transaction (Account, LOCAL AuthIdentity, AccountRole) still goes through the real `TypeOrmUnitOfWork`/real repositories against real Postgres, so the rollback this test observes is genuine, not simulated (c) was rejected because it can't reliably target 'the last step' deterministically and would couple the test to incidental constraint shapes rather than the actual step being exercised.

decisions.decision: Captured the transaction's generated `accountId` by having the overriding `USER_PROFILE_PROVISIONER` mock record `input.accountId` (the field `CreateAccountUseCase` already passes to `userProfileProvisioner.provision(...)`) before rejecting, instead of intercepting `ID_GENERATOR` or trying to look up the row by phone after the fact.
decisions.reason: `CreateAccountUseCase.execute` never returns an `accountId` on failure (it throws before reaching its `return` statement), and `Account`/`AccountRole` don't store the phone directly, so there is no other reliable handle to query those two tables by after a forced failure. The mock already receives the exact `accountId` that transaction used as a normal part of its real call contract (`ProvisionUserProfileInput.accountId`) — reusing that value needs no extra indirection (no `ID_GENERATOR` spy/wrapper) and ties the assertion to the same identifier the production code itself operated on.

decisions.decision: Exported `ACCOUNT_REPOSITORY`/`AccountRepository` and `AUTH_IDENTITY_REPOSITORY`/`AuthIdentityRepository` from `libs/modules/identity-access/src/public-api.ts`, and `USER_PROFILE_REPOSITORY`/`UserProfileRepository` from `libs/modules/user-profiles/src/public-api.ts`, purely so the new e2e spec can resolve them via `moduleRef.get(TOKEN, { strict: false })`.
decisions.reason: `ACCOUNT_ROLE_REPOSITORY` and `ROLE_REPOSITORY` were already exported from identity-access's `public-api.ts` for exactly this reason (consumed by `apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts`'s existing test-setup helpers) — this follows that established precedent rather than reaching past the module boundary with a deep relative import (which `no-cross-module-internal-import` in `.dependency-cruiser.js` would in any case only enforce for files under `libs/modules/*/src`, not for `apps/api/test/*`, but deep-importing from a different app would still be inconsistent with how every other e2e spec in this codebase obtains module internals).

assumptions: The shared throwaway Postgres/Redis/MinIO test infra (memories-test-postgres/redis/minio, already running via docker) is the intended real-infrastructure target for migration and e2e validation, per docs/guides referenced from .env's own header comment.

AC36/AC39's frontend-facing clauses and task.md §18 remain out of scope for this epic per changes/cycle-001/requirement-addendum.md's backend-only decision; this cycle only re-verifies the backend halves (Swagger reflects real endpoints; mock authentication removed from backend).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:module-boundary
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Identity access and user profile responsibilities are separated into identity-access and user-profiles modules; public APIs/application contracts are used across modules, and npm run test:architecture plus the Nest wiring/port-binding checks pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:account-domain-model
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The Account aggregate, status and token-version behavior, persistence mapping, protected-request status checks, CRUD use cases and unit/E2E coverage are implemented; locked, deleted and password-changed accounts are rejected by current-session checks.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:authidentity-model
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AuthIdentity domain and persistence layers support the declared providers while fully implementing LOCAL phone/password authentication, normalized unique identifiers and password hashing; credentials are excluded from API responses and covered by unit/E2E tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:userprofile-domain-model
acceptance_criteria.evidence: UserProfile is implemented across domain/application/infrastructure/presentation layers with unique account ownership, normalized optional email, date-only persistence conversion and no cross-module TypeORM relation; CRUD and dateOfBirth E2E paths pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:customer-v-staff-boundary
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Account creation provisions only UserProfile and does not create Customer or Staff; module-boundary documentation distinguishes the shared profile from future Customer/Staff business records, and architecture validation passes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:auditable-entity-foundation
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Shared auditable props and ORM audit columns are implemented with timezone-aware timestamps and soft-delete metadata; client DTOs cannot provide audit fields, and mutation use cases obtain actors from RequestContext.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:database-migration
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Identity and profile migrations, indexes/constraints and idempotent RBAC seed are present; migration run, revert and re-run all passed against the real test PostgreSQL instance.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:transaction-t-o-account
acceptance_criteria.evidence: CreateAccountUseCase performs normalized-phone validation, password hashing, Account/AuthIdentity/UserProfile creation and default-role assignment in one UnitOfWork transaction; rollback and duplicate-phone tests pass, and registration reuses this transaction. Attempt 5: closed a TOCTOU gap where the preflight duplicate-phone check could race under real concurrency — TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save() now translates the database's own unique-constraint violation into the same DomainError.conflict the preflight check throws, so the transaction still rolls back cleanly and the caller now reliably gets 409 instead of an occasional 500; proven by a new real-Postgres concurrent-registration e2e test.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:login-b-ng-phone-v-password
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Login accepts phone/password/portal, normalizes Vietnamese phone numbers, authenticates through LOCAL, checks account state and portal permission before issuing a session, rejects email fallback and avoids account enumeration; auth E2E tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:ph-n-bi-t-authentication-v-authorization
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Credential validation and account resolution are separated from permission-based portal authorization; login does not hard-code roles and no token/session is issued before the requested portal permission succeeds.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:authentication-provider-abstraction
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AuthenticationProvider and supporting ports isolate provider-specific validation from login/session/JWT logic; LOCAL is implemented without adding provider switches to the login use case, and port-binding validation passes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:rbac-foundation
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Role, Permission, AccountRole and RolePermission domain/persistence foundations, stable permission codes, configurable default role, permission evaluator and guarded Account/UserProfile APIs are implemented; seed idempotency and authorization tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:jwt-payload-v-session
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Access tokens and refresh sessions carry account, profile, session, portal and provider context; refresh rotation is attempt-safe, PUBLIC tokens are rejected by ADMIN APIs, and live account/tokenVersion checks invalidate issued access tokens after security changes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:request-context
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Async request context captures request/auth metadata without passing HTTP requests into application code; guards enrich the context, system execution is supported, and concurrent-request E2E coverage confirms isolation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: slice:audit-behavior

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC46: Đăng ký với phone đã tồn tại trả về lỗi nghiệp vụ rõ ràng, không tạo Account trùng, không rollback một phần
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Fixed in response to fix-request-review-3.md's major finding (previously `failed` — the sequential-duplicate e2e test only submitted the second registration after the first had already committed, so it never exercised the actual race: two concurrent registrations for the same phone could both pass CreateAccountUseCase's `existsByProviderAndIdentifier` preflight check before either committed, and the loser then received a generic HTTP 500 from GlobalExceptionFilter instead of the required 409 business error, because TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save() let the database's raw QueryFailedError unique-violation propagate unchanged). Fixed by adding TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.translateUniqueViolation(): it catches QueryFailedError, matches Postgres SQLSTATE 23505 against the named constraint UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier, and translates a match into the same DomainError.conflict('phone_already_exists', ...) the preflight check already throws — GlobalExceptionFilter still maps this to 409 as before, and UnitOfWork.withTransaction still rolls back the loser's transaction cleanly since the fix only rethrows a different, better-typed error. New e2e test (apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts, 'lets exactly one of two concurrent registrations for the same phone succeed, rejecting the other with a 409 business error and no partial state') fires two concurrent POST /auth/register requests with the same phone against the real Postgres-backed AppModule, asserts response statuses are exactly [201, 409] (never 500) with the loser's body carrying errorCode 'phone_already_exists', confirms via the real AuthIdentityRepository/UserProfileRepository/AccountRoleRepository/AccountRepository that the winner has exactly one committed AuthIdentity/UserProfile/AccountRole/Account graph, and confirms the winner's credentials work end to end via a subsequent login. The original sequential-duplicate e2e test (same describe block) continues to pass unchanged.

RegisterDto now derives its password @MinLength/@MaxLength from the new shared PASSWORD_POLICY constant (libs/modules/identity-access/src/domain/value-objects/password-policy.ts), identically to CreateAccountDto and ChangeAccountPasswordDto; RegisterUseCase delegates to CreateAccountUseCase, whose execute() now calls assertPasswordPolicy(input.password) before hashing — enforced at the application/domain boundary, not only by the DTO — so a caller invoking the use case directly (bypassing the DTO) still can't persist an out-of-policy password. Required phone/password/fullName, optional validated+length-limited email, and the global ThrottlerGuard (APP_GUARD) rate-limiting the route identically to /auth/login are all still in place. Evidence: password-policy.spec.ts (boundary tests + no-echo-in-error test), create-account.use-case.spec.ts 'rejects and creates nothing when the password violates the centralized password policy', change-account-password.use-case.spec.ts 'rejects and persists nothing when the new password violates the centralized password policy' (new spec file, this use case had no unit test before), and e2e 'rejects registration missing required fields' (400).
